findings.summary: The contract says to update the user-scoped and current project-scoped Claude installations, but requires one scope-less update command for the agent.
findings.evidence: The brief says both a user-scoped installation and a project-scoped one are updated (lines 163-166), while lines 161-162 require exactly `<agent> plugin update vloop@vloop` once. `docs/design-notes/copilot-cli-experiments.md` lines 819-825 records that the same Claude plugin id can appear once per project and that update accepts `--scope`; it does not establish that scope auto-detection updates every counted installation. The contract therefore has two reachable implementations: update only the auto-detected installation, or update each installation with explicit scopes.
findings.fix: Decide whether self-update updates every counted Claude scope or only the active/auto-detected installation. If every scope, specify the literal command(s), their ordering and the plugin output/JSON result when one scope succeeds and another fails; if only one, narrow the "what is updated" rule to that installation.

findings.summary: The brief claims to reuse doctor's Claude matching rule but excludes local-scoped entries.
findings.evidence: The brief at lines 157-160 counts only `scope: user`/empty or `scope: project` with a matching project path. `internal/cli/doctor.go` lines 812-818 starts with user/empty and otherwise accepts any entry whose non-empty `projectPath` matches the root; it does not restrict that branch to `project`. B36's rule also covers the latter scope-bearing forms.
findings.fix: Use the doctor's literal rule: count user or empty scope, otherwise count an entry with a project path matching this root (including local scope), and add a local-scope worked example.

decisions: Use `vloop self-update`; keep repository `vloop upgrade` unchanged. I agree: the command names separate machine and repository concerns.
Use the Go module proxy/toolchain as the release channel. I agree: it matches the documented install path and avoids a second release API.
Install only a strictly newer release unless `--version` explicitly names an older or prerelease target. I agree.
Refuse checkout builds, a missing Go toolchain, and a binary/install-directory mismatch rather than install where PATH may not find it. I agree.
Keep doctor and `vloop upgrade` offline; self-update alone may use the network. I agree.
Report plugin failures without failing a run in which the binary step succeeded. I agree, with the scope behavior above pinned first.
Make C-2 path formatting allow this repository-less command to print home-relative, slash-normalized external paths. I agree.
Use temporary Go fake programs for external tools in tests. I agree.
Use `golang.org/x/mod/semver` with no new dependency. I agree.
Allow `--check` with `--version` to compare against the requested target. I agree.
checked: facts, consistency, rules, runnability; inspected the dependency brief, domain/platform rules, roadmap, guide, build-info, doctor, release tooling and plugin experiment record; a ready copy passes `vloop brief check` except for the expected unresolved new schema path.
